chunks: The act of generosity (al-ma'ruf) when given to those not entitled to it

He who shows generosity to those who have no claim to it or who are not fit for it would not earn anything except the praise of the ignoble and appreciation of bad persons, although as long as he continues giving, the ignorant will say how generous his hand is, even though in the affairs of Allāh he is a miser.

key_terms.الْمَعْرُوف: Generosity / Kindness / The act of doing good

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of giving charity or generosity to the unworthy?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi presents this passage as a critique of *al-ma'ruf* (generosity/goodness) when directed at the unworthy, warning that such misplaced charity yields only the superficial praise of the ignorant and the ignoble. It highlights a spiritual paradox: the giver appears generous to people but remains miserly in the affairs of Allah, failing to invest in true spiritual worth. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on discerning the recipient's merit to ensure charity serves as a means of divine closeness rather than mere social transaction.

en.sayed-ali-raza: He who shows generosity to those who have no claim to it or who are not fit for it would not earn anything except the praise of the ignoble and appreciation of bad persons, although as long as he continues giving, the ignorant will say how generous his hand is, even though in the affairs of Allāh he is a miser.
